title: Mustard Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Mustard Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Mustard nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, sulfur and potassium in mustasa, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Mustard nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your mustasa (mustard) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, sulfur, potassium, phosphorus, boron, magnesium and calcium. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Potassium deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for mustard

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But sulfur, boron and calcium stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which mustard nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a mustard nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest mustard nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in mustard

Older leaves turn yellow green first, then the whole plant pales. Some leaves get reddish or orange tints and dry patches. Leaves keep their shape but stay small, growth slows and plants may bolt early. You see it most at this stage: from transplanting to harvest.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in mustasa
Sandy soils, heavy rain or watering, low organic matter and too little nitrogen for a fast leafy crop.
How to tell it apart
Sulfur shortage, very common in mustard, starts on the young leaves instead. Purple color in some mustard varieties is normal. To be sure, old leaves yellow first. Soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress or drench with urea or ammonium sulfate in small weekly doses based on the soil test. KAU gives a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water for cole crops.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add manure or compost at bed preparation and feed weekly.
Sulfur deficiency in mustard

Plants are small and spindly. Young and middle leaves turn pale between the veins while the veins stand out blue green, the leaves cup and become brittle. The undersides turn purple or bronze. Symptoms develop slowly. You see it most at this stage: early growth on light soils after heavy rain.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in mustasa
Light, sandy soils with low organic matter, wet weather that leaches sulfate, and fertilizer programs of urea and muriate of potash only. Mustard and other brassicas need a lot of sulfur.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage starts on the older, lower leaves. To be sure, A leaf tissue test is the most reliable check, since sulfate leaches and soil tests can mislead.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency

Use ammonium sulfate or gypsum. Teagasc advises about 20 kg of sulfur per hectare for brassica vegetables on light soils (roughly 85 kg ammonium sulfate per hectare). In a field trial on Indian mustard grown for seed, gypsum gave better yields than single superphosphate as the sulfur source.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use some sulfur fertilizer every crop.
Potassium deficiency in mustard
The edges of older leaves yellow and then turn light brown and dry, and the dead band spreads inward. Leaf edges curl upward and growth slows. You see it most at this stage: mid growth to harvest.
Why potassium deficiency happens in mustasa
Sandy or acid soils, heavy rain or watering, and fertilizing with urea only.
How to tell it apart
Fertilizer burn appears suddenly after a strong feed. Potassium shortage builds slowly on the old leaves. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Apply complete fertilizer or muriate of potash based on the soil test. For a quick fix, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water for cabbage, a close relative.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use complete fertilizer at bed preparation.
Phosphorus deficiency in mustard

Plants grow slowly and stay small. Older leaves can turn dark, then reddish or purple from the edges, often on the undersides. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth, in cold or dry soil.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in mustasa
Acid or iron rich soils, low organic matter, cold, wet or dry soil, and no phosphorus at planting.
How to tell it apart
Some mustard varieties are naturally purple. Nitrogen shortage gives pale rather than dark leaves. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply complete 14 14 14 or 16 20 0 at planting based on the soil test. KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick correction in cole crops.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a phosphorus fertilizer and manure at bed preparation.
Boron deficiency in mustard

Young leaves stay small, curl and become deformed, with yellow mottling along the edges. Leaf stalks and midribs can crack or turn corky, and in severe cases the growing point dies. You see it most at this stage: mid growth.
Why boron deficiency happens in mustasa
Sandy soils, overlimed or alkaline soils, low organic matter and drought. Brassicas need more boron than most crops.
How to tell it apart
Aphids also curl young leaves. Look for insects. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for boron deficiency
For cole crops, KAU gives borax at about 10 kg per hectare in the soil or a spray at 1 gram per liter of water. Do not repeat without a test.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add a small dose of borax to the basal fertilizer on sandy beds.
Magnesium deficiency in mustard

Older leaves yellow between the veins, starting at the edges and moving toward the midrib, while the veins stay green. Yellow areas may later turn orange, red or brown. You see it most at this stage: mid growth to harvest.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in mustasa
Acid sandy soils, soils high in potassium, heavy potash fertilizer and heavy rain.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf. To be sure, soil test for magnesium, potassium and pH.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
Spray magnesium sulfate for quick relief. For cole crops KAU gives magnesium sulfate in a band at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre). Do not apply it together with potash.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soil.
Calcium deficiency in mustard
The tips and edges of young, fast growing leaves die and turn brown, and the damage spreads inward. Rot can enter the damaged tissue. You see it most at this stage: fast growth in hot, dry spells.
Why calcium deficiency happens in mustasa
Uneven watering and fast growth, acid sandy soils, and heavy ammonium or potash.
How to tell it apart
Bacterial rots start wet. Tip burn starts as dry dead edges. To be sure, soil test for calcium and pH.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
Water evenly. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid beds before planting and keep watering steady.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any mustard nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your mustasa needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Mustard nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my mustasa leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves turn pale yellow, sometimes with red tints, and leaves stay small. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at sulfur deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in mustard?
items.a: Side dress or drench with urea or ammonium sulfate in small weekly doses based on the soil test. KAU gives a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water for cole crops.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes sulfur deficiency in mustard?
items.a: Use ammonium sulfate or gypsum. Teagasc advises about 20 kg of sulfur per hectare for brassica vegetables on light soils (roughly 85 kg ammonium sulfate per hectare).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in mustard?
items.a: Apply complete fertilizer or muriate of potash based on the soil test. For a quick fix, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water for cabbage, a close relative.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my mustasa lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the mustard nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
